'''Gulf South Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name=source1>[https://www.gulfsouthpl.com/about-us/subsidiaries/gulf-south-pipeline-company-lp/default.aspx Gulf South Gas Pipeline,] Gulf South Pipeline, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs between points in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.

==Background==

=== Main Line ===
The Gulf South Gas Pipeline is owned and operated by the Gulf South Gas Pipeline Company LP, a subsidiary of Boardwalk Pipeline Partners.<ref name=source1/> Boardwalk Pipeline Partners is owned by Loews Corporation. The pipeline gathers gas from basins in Texas and Alabama and delivers it to the U.S. Northeast, Midwest and Southeast.<ref name=source1/>

==== Pipeline explosion ====<!--{{#ev:youtube|Yl4tzvAvbGY|500|right|Gas pipeline explodes at Ross Barnett Reservoir in Mississippi.|frame}}-->
In January 2015, a section of the pipeline that goes under the Barnett Reservoir near Brandon, MS, exploded.<ref name="WAPT">[http://www.wapt.com/article/gas-line-explodes-burns-near-reservoir/2091806 Gas line explodes, burns near reservoir], WAPT, Jan. 14, 2015, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref> "I thought it was a tornado coming through, or something, because it got to shaking the house," said one resident. "There was just a loud explosion at first and then the house started shaking." Photographs of the fire caused by the explosion can be seen on local Jackson, Mississippi news.<ref name="WAPT" />

=== GS Bastian Bay Extension ===
The extension is located in Louisiana.<ref name=":1" /> The construction of the project was completed in November 1997.<ref name=":1" />

=== GS Gulfstream Interconnect ===
This expansion was completed in 2002, adding 29 miles of pipeline and 236 MMcf/d of capacity in Alabama.<ref name=":1" />

=== GS Southeast Expansion ===
Boardwalk Pipeline Partners proposed the project in August 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.naturalgasintel.com/gulf-south-has-southeastern-expansion-plans/|title=Gulf South Has Southeastern Expansion Plans|last=|first=|date=26 April, 2006|website=Natural Gas Intel|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> The expansion project gives Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas and Louisiana natural gas supplies greater access to Northeast, Florida and other Southeast markets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.naturalgasintel.com/gulf-souths-southeast-expansion-enters-service/|title=Gulf South’s Southeast Expansion Enters Service|last=|first=|date=03 June, 2008|website=Natural Gas Intel|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> The project provides producers in eastern Texas and northern Louisiana a more eastern outlet for a portion of their production from the Barnett Shale, Bossier Sand and other fields that are being delivered in the Perryville, Louisiana area or the central Mississippi area and permit deliveries into the Florida markets via an interconnect with Destin Gas Transmission and into Northeast markets via the interconnect at Transco’s Compressor Station 85.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2006-09-11/pdf/E6-14980.pdf|title=FERC Register|last=|first=|date=11 September, 2006|website=Gov Info|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> The construction of the project was completed in June 2008.<ref name=":1" />

=== GS Texas to Mississippi Expansion ===
In September 2006, Gulf South filed an application before U.S. FERC for authorization to construct and operate the project, which connects Gulf South's existing facilities in Keatchie, DeSoto Parish, Louisiana to Gulf South's pipeline in Simpson County, Mississippi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2007/07/13/E7-13644/east-texas-to-mississippi-expansion-project-gulf-south-pipeline-company-lp-federal-energy-regulatory|title=Federal Register :: Request Access|website=www.federalregister.gov|language=en|access-date=2023-09-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1262943/000119312506238043/d424b4.htm|title=Boardwalk Pipelines, LP: Prospectus|last=|first=|date=16 November, 2006|website=U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> FERC approved the project that provided takeaway capacity for producers in Barnett Shale and Bossier Sands of East Texas in June 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.naturalgasintel.com/gulf-south-ready-to-start-remainder-of-east-texas-mississippi-expansion/|title=Gulf South Ready to Start Remainder of East Texas-Mississippi Expansion|last=|first=|date=17 January, 2008|website=Natural Gas Intel|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref>  The construction of the expansion project was completed in June 2008.<ref name=":1" />

=== GS Mobile Compressor Expansion ===
The construction of the project was completed in August 2008.<ref name=":1" />

=== GS Gulf Crossing Mississippi Loop ===
The expansion is located in Mississippi. The construction of the project was completed in December 2008.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.naturalgasintel.com/gulf-crossings-mississippi-loop-set-to-open-dec-29/|title=Gulf Crossing’s Mississippi Loop Set to Open Dec. 29|last=|first=|date=24 December, 2008|website=Natural Gas Intel|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref>

=== Haynesville/Perryville Expansion ===
The project consisted of adding compression facilities to the Hall Summit Compressor station, Haynesville, Louisiana and Tallulah Compressor station, Perryville, Louisiana.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1336047/000133604709000026/exhibit99_1.htm|title=Boardwalk Pipeline Partners: Investor Presentation|last=|first=|date=May 2009|website=U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> The construction of the project was completed in October 2010.'''<ref name=":1" />'''

=== Southeast Market Expansion ===
In August 2012, Gulf South received binding commitments for the project and completed the open season.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1336047/000133604712000032/exh992bwpsemarketpressrele.htm|title=Boardwalk's Gulf South Pipeline announces Southeast Market Expansion project|last=|first=|date=19 August, 2012|website=U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> In August 2013, FERC had prepared the environmental assessment report for the project.<ref name=":3" /> The project was completed in October, 2014.<ref name=":1" /> The project connects natural gas supplies in northern Louisiana with markets in the southeast US. The project uses both Boardwalk’s Perryville Hub and its Petal gas storage capacity.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/17272987/boardwalk-advances-southeast-market-expansion-gas-line-project|title=Boardwalk advances Southeast Market Expansion gas line project|last=Smith|first=Christopher E.|date=20 August, 2023|website=Oil & Gas Journal|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref> The project added transmission capacity to the Gulf South system from multiple locations in Texas and Louisiana to Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.annualreports.com/HostedData/AnnualReportArchive/b/NYSE_BWP_2012.pdf|title=Boardwalk Pipeline Partners: 2012 Annual report|last=|first=|date=2012|website=Annual reports|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=11 September, 2023}}</ref>

=== Coastal Bend Header Pipeline ===
In June 2015 Gulf South Pipeline applied to FERC to build the Coastal Bend Header Pipeline in Wharton and Brazoria Counties, TX.<ref name="oilman">[https://oilmanmagazine.com/article/gulf-south-pipeline-submits-application-for-coastal-bend-header-project/ Gulf South Pipeline Submits Application For Coastal Bend Header Project], Oilman,  accessed January 2018</ref> Gulf South received FERC approval in Jun 2016,<ref name="FERC">[https://www.ferc.gov/CalendarFiles/20160620165309-CP15-517-000.pdf ORDER ISSUING CERTIFICATE, Docket No. CP15-517-000], FERC, Jun. 20, 2016</ref> and began construction of the pipeline in April 2017.<ref>[http://www.gulfsouthpl.com/ExpansionProjects.aspx?id=4294967461 Coastal Bend Header Pipeline and Metering Facilities – Notice to Proceed], Gulf South Pipeline, accessed January 2018</ref> The project would include seven new interconnects with various interstate and intrastate pipelines, including the Gulf South Pipeline.<ref name="oilman" /> Gulf South Pipeline estimated the construction costs of the pipeline to be approximately US$690 million.<ref>Barry Cassell, [https://www.transmissionhub.com/articles/2015/06/ferc-begins-review-of-690m-coastal-bend-pipeline-project-of-gulf-south.html "FERC begins review of $690m Coastal Bend pipeline project of Gulf South"], Transmission Hub, Jun. 26, 2015</ref>

In May of 2018, the Coastal Bend Header gas pipeline was put into service. The first phase delivered 0.7 billion cubic feet (bcf) of natural gas per day to the [[Freeport LNG Terminal]] export facility. The second phase, completed in November of 2018, delivers an additional 0.7 bcf.<ref name="service">[https://finance.yahoo.com/news/boardwalk-pipeline-partners-apos-days-140800694.html Are Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' Days as a Public Company Numbered?], Yahoo Finance,  May 5, 2018</ref>
===Westlake Expansion Project===
The project was designed to provide gas for a 994-MW Entergy Louisiana LLC gas-fired, combined-cycle electric generation plant, the Lake Charles Power Station, for an initial term of 20 years.<ref name=":4" /> In July 2017, Gulf South filed an application before FERC for authorization to construct and operate the Westlake expansion project.<ref name=":5" /> In February 2018, FERC completed the environmental assessment of the project and passed approval for the project.<ref name=":4" /> The construction of the project was completed in August 2019.'''<ref name=":1" />'''

===Willis Lateral Expansion Project===
The expansion pipeline was proposed to supply 1 GW worth of energy to the Willis combined Cycle power plant.<ref name=":1" /> The pipeline starts in Texas and ends at the Willis combined Cycle power plant in Texas, USA.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="ftmap">[https://www.fractracker.org/2020/02/national-energy-petrochemical-map/ National Energy and Petrochemical Map], FracTracker, Feb. 28, 2020, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

It began operations on May 31, 2020.<ref name="op" />
===Index 99 Expansion Project===
In March 2020, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) authorized construction and operation of Gulf South Pipeline Co.’s proposed Index 99 Expansion project, which would increase natural gas firm transportation to markets along the Gulf Coast. The project would provide 500 million cubic feet per day of natural gas firm transportation service to markets along the Gulf Coast and provide an additional 250 million cubic feet per day of capacity to existing facilities in northern Louisiana. All of the project’s components would be in Texas and Louisiana, which include installing about 22 miles of 30-inch diameter pipeline (Index 99L) in San Augustine and Sabine counties in Texas, installing a pig receiver at the intersection of the new Index 99L pipeline and Gulf South’s existing Index 99 system in San Augustine County, as well as installing 250 feet of 24-inch diameter station pipe and a 24-inch diameter pressure control valve at the Hall Summit compressor station in Bienville Parish, LA.<ref name="exp">David Bradley, [https://www.naturalgasintel.com/ferc-approves-gulf-souths-index-99-natural-gas-expansion/ FERC Approves Gulf South’s Index 99 Natural Gas Expansion], Natural Gas Intel, Mar. 20, 2020, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref> The Index 99 expansion project was commissioned on Aug. 31, 2020.<ref>[https://www.bwpipelines.com/about-us/subsidiaries/gulf-south-pipeline-company-lp/expansions/current-projects/index-99/timeline-and-updates/2019/Gulf-South-Files-Index-99-Expansion-FERC-Application/default.aspx INDEX 99 TIMELINE], Boardwalk Pipelines, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

The expansion will run through San Augustine and Sabine counties in Texas, to Bienville Parish, LA.<ref name="exp" />
===McComb Compressor Station Reliability Project===
The project involves replacing a compressor station in southern Mississippi, resulting in an increase in transmission capacity.<ref name=":1" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, construction was completed in March 2021.<ref name=":1" />
===Lamar County Expansion Project===
The expansion project will add natural gas delivery of up to 200,000 dekatherms per day to the Morrow Repower Project, a new 550 MW combined cycle power plant developed by Cooperative Energy Texas in Mississippi, USA.<ref name=":0">https://s2.q4cdn.com/221564406/files/doc_downloads/2019/Vol_I_LamarCountyExpanApp.pdf Accessed on 01 August, 2023</ref> The Morrow Repower Project is replacing a coal plant.<ref name=":1" /> 

The Lamar County Expansion Project entailed the construction, operation and maintenance of a gas pipeline, setting up an new delivery meter station, and setting up an new 5,000 hp compressor station called the Black Creek Compressor station.<ref name=":0" />

In June 2020, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) issued order approving the construction and operation of the project. The project was completed and began operation from December 2021.<ref>https://s2.q4cdn.com/221564406/files/doc_downloads/south_pipeline/Lamar/Lamar-County-Expansion-Project-In-Service-Notification.pdf Accessed on 01 August, 2023</ref>

=== PLUSS Project ===
The Parks Line Upgrade and Sorrento Station Project was announced in 2024. It is a pipeline replacement and compressor station construction project. It includes replacing segments of Gulf South's 30-inch diameter pipeline in St. Martin Parish, Louisiana, and the construction of a new compressor station (Sorrento Compressor Station) in Ascension Parish, Louisiana. It plans to be in service by 2028.<ref name=":7" />

=== Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project ===
Project is to replace existing reciprocating compressor units in Acadia Parish, LA, and to install over pressure protection at the existing Woodlawn Junction in Jefferson Davis Parish, LA. Project will create 120,000 Dth/d of additional capacity into the Lake Charles area. The environmental assessment was completed in January 2025.<ref name=":1" />

=== Kosci Junction Project ===
The Project entails constructing approximately 102 miles of new 36-inch pipe from Attala to Clarke counties, MS, approximately 8 miles of new 36-inch pipe in Humphreys & Sunflower counties, MS. The project also includes the new Kosci Compressor Station in Attala County, MS and the new Holmes Compressor Station in Holmes County, MS, as well as modifications to the company’s existing Greenville Compressor Station in Washington County, MS and Isola Compressor Station in Humphreys County, MS.<ref name=":1" />

=== Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion Project ===
Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion Project (Project). The Project consists of adding additional compression at three existing compressor stations in Madison Parish, LA, Jasper and Forrest Counties, MS, and construct one new greenfield compressor station in Hinds County.<ref name=":1" />
